newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fokker, Samsung decision "within days" - Dutch govt.
newsitem.headline: Fokker, Samsung decision "within days" - Dutch govt.

text.p: Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers said on Tuesday he expected a decision on a takeover of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker NV by South Korea's Samsung Aerospace within days," news agency ANP said.

Wijers earlier met Dutch cabinet colleagues to inform them of the progress of protracted negotiations between Samsung, the Dutch government and Fokker administrators. But he declined to speculate on the possible outcome of the talks.
No-one at the ministry was immediately available to comment.

Court-appointed administrators have been running Fokker since it was declared bankrupt in March. Two months ago they gave Samsung exclusive rights to examine Fokker's books with a view to bidding for its core aircraft-making business.
Samsung, which sees Fokker as a way of breaking into the global aerospace industry, is unwilling to assume all the risks and wants major investment by the Dutch state.

The Hague has said it would provide capital and invest in a new 125-seat regional jet, but Samsung is said to have baulked at demands for long-term job guarantees in the Netherlands, where labour costs are higher than the Far East.

Fokker, founded in 1919 by Dutch aviation pioneer Anthony Fokker, is one of the oldest names in the industry and its F27 Friendship turboprop, launched in 1957, was one of the industry's biggest commercial successes. But in more recent years Fokker struggled to achieve financial stability and swapped industry partners several times. In 1993, Daimler Benz Aerospace [DAIG.F] (DASA) paid 686 million guilders for a 51 percent stake in Fokker, but depressed world aircraft markets and a weak dollar saw the company sink into deep losses that had to be met by DASA and the Dutch state.
In January 1996, Daimler cut off all financial support, forcing the company into bankruptcy in March. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040 REUTER
